rules.title: Security deposit cap, handling, interest, and return
rules.requirement: A landlord may not take a security deposit larger than the first month's rent. The deposit must be kept in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account and the landlord must give receipts and a statement of condition and pay 5% interest (or the lesser bank rate) each year. The landlord must return the deposit within 30 days after the tenancy ends, minus only unpaid rent or water charges, tax escalation amounts, and itemized damage. Breaking these rules means the landlord loses the right to keep any of the deposit and can owe treble damages. The state housing office may allow an optional fee in place of a deposit, but the fee plus any deposit may not total more than 1 month's rent.

coverage.notes: The cap and return rules apply to residential leases and tenancies. Successor owners are responsible for transferred deposits, except cities or towns that take title under chapter 60 and foreclosing mortgagees that are state- or federally-chartered financial institutions.

rules.coverage_text: Leases of residential real property and the landlords (and their successors in interest) who accept security deposits.
rules.exemptions: Vacation or recreational leases or rentals of 100 days or less.
rules.interaction: Any lease provision that conflicts with this section, and any tenant waiver of it, is void and unenforceable.
rules.quoted_span: No lessor or successor in interest shall at any time subsequent to the commencement of a tenancy demand rent in advance in excess of the current month's rent or a security deposit in excess of the amount allowed by this section.

rules.title: Cap on upfront payments at start of tenancy (text before Aug. 1, 2025)
rules.requirement: At or before the start of a tenancy, a landlord may not require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay more than first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit equal to the first month's rent, and the cost of buying and installing a key and lock.
